\tabnotes{For each country and maturity $n\in\{2,5,10\}$ years, the one-year
  excess return $\rx^{(n)}_{i,t+12}$ is regressed on the local
  Cochrane--Piazzesi factor $\CP_{i,t}$ alone (Local); on the GDP-weighted
  global factor $\GCP_{t}$ alone (Global); and on both jointly (Joint), where
  the local factor is first orthogonalised with respect to the global one
  (denoted $\CP^{\perp}_{i,t}$) so that its coefficient measures the
  incremental local content---the forward-factor analogue of the horse race
  \eqref{eq:h-horse}--\eqref{eq:h-global}. Adjusted $R^{2}$ is reported for
  each specification; the Wald $p$-value in brackets tests the joint
  significance of the two slopes in the joint regression. All inference is
  Newey--West adjusted ($12$ lags). The table replicates
  \citet{dahlquist2013}, Table~6.}
